content.title: Recommendations for the diagnosis and treatment of chronic heart failure (HF)

Recommendations for the diagnosis of chr: Routine blood tests for comorbidities (full blood count, urea and electrolytes, thyroid function, fasting glucose and HbA1c, lipids, iron studies [TSAT and ferritin])
Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) recommended for assessment of myocardial structure and function and for characterization of myocardial tissue in suspected infiltrative disease or myocarditis
Invasive coronary angiography recommended in patients with angina despite therapy or symptomatic ventricular arrhythmias
Cardiopulmonary exercise testing recommended as part of evaluation for heart transplantation/MCS
Right heart catheterization recommended in patients with severe HF being evaluated for transplantation or MCS
Recommendations for the treatment of HFr: ACE inhibitors (ACE‑I) recommended to reduce risk of HF hospitalization and death
Beta-blockers recommended to reduce risk of HF hospitalization and death
Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRA) recommended to reduce risk of HF hospitalization and death
SGLT2 inhibitors (dapagliflozin or empagliflozin) recommended to reduce risk of HF hospitalization and death
Sacubitril/valsartan recommended as replacement for ACE‑I in patients with HFrEF to reduce risk of HF hospitalization and death
Diuretics recommended for symptom relief in patients with congestion
ARB recommended to reduce risk of HF hospitalization and CV death in patients intolerant of ACE‑I
Combination of ACE‑I and MRA is not recommended in patients with HF because of increased risk of renal dysfunction and hyperkalaemia (unless specific situations noted)

Implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) recommended to reduce risk of sudden death and all-cause mortality in selected patients with recovered ventricular arrhythmia risk, or symptomatic HF with LVEF ≤35% despite OMT with expected survival >1 year
Cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) recommended in selected patients with symptomatic HF in sinus rhythm with QRS ≥150 ms and LBBB QRS morphology and LVEF ≤35% despite OMT
Recommendations regarding ICD/CRT implantation timing, ischemic etiology, and specific QRS indications are noted (see full guideline)
Recommendations for the treatment of HFm: Diuretics recommended for patients with congestion to alleviate symptoms and signs
